title: iterate-review reviewer output
description: Structured output from Codex reviewing a code diff via the iterate-review skill. Enforced by codex exec --output-schema. All four top-level array fields are required-but-may-be-empty.

verdict.description: APPROVE = code is structurally sound, ready to ship; REVISE = at least one load-bearing issue to fix; BLOCK = fundamental problem that invalidates the change's premise (rare).

findings.description: Substantive issues with the code change. Required field; may be empty if verdict=APPROVE with nothing to flag.

severity.description: HIGH = load-bearing, would cause incorrect behavior or break invariants if shipped; always blocks APPROVE. MEDIUM = real issue worth addressing; doesn't block APPROVE if Opus disputes/explains, but considered. LOW = nit, polish, stylistic.

description.description: Full text of the issue. Cite file paths and line numbers from the diff when useful (e.g., 'web/lib/foo.ts:42 introduces an unguarded null deref'). Be concrete.

suggested_action.description: What Opus should consider doing about it. May be open-ended ('clarify the contract') or specific ('add a null check before line 42'). Describe intent, not the literal patch text.

code_corrections.description: Tactical non-controversial fixes (typos in comments, broken imports, dead code, contradictions between docstring and behavior). Required; may be empty. Distinct from findings in that corrections are mechanical and Opus should incorporate them without dispute.

location.description: File path with line number when known (e.g., 'web/app/page.tsx:120', 'pipeline/foo.py:fn_name'). For changes spanning multiple lines, use a range or the function/section name.

fix.description: What it should be, in abstract terms. Opus does the actual edit.

new_questions.description: Questions Codex wants the user (via Opus) to answer in the next pass — typically clarifications about author intent or constraints not visible in the diff. Required; may be empty.
